column3: In trunk-based development, each developer divides their own work into small batches and merges that work into trunk at least once, and potentially several times, a day (`dora-capabilities-trunk#searchLinkMobile`).
column5: The second pattern is known as trunk-based development, where each developer divides their own work into small batches and merges that work into trunk at least once (and potentially several times) a day.

column3: Feature branches typically involve multiple developers and take days or even weeks of work (`dora-capabilities-trunk#searchLinkMobile`).
column5: Feature branches typically involve multiple developers and take days or even weeks of work.

column3: Branches in trunk-based development typically last no more than a few hours, with many developers merging their individual changes into trunk frequently (`dora-capabilities-trunk#searchLinkMobile`).
column5: In contrast, branches in trunk-based development typically last no more than a few hours, with many developers merging their individual changes into trunk frequently.

column3: In cases where releases happen multiple times a day, release branches are not required at all, because changes can be pushed directly into trunk and deployed from there (`dora-capabilities-trunk#searchLinkMobile`).
column5: In cases where releases happen multiple times a day, release branches are not required at all, because changes can be pushed directly into trunk and deployed from there.

column3: Trunk-based development is a required practice for continuous integration (`dora-capabilities-trunk#how-to-implement-trunk-based-development`).
column5: Trunk-based development is a required practice for continuous integration.

column3: Continuous integration (CI) is the combination of practicing trunk-based development and maintaining a suite of fast automated tests that run after each commit to trunk to make sure the system is always working (`dora-capabilities-trunk#how-to-implement-trunk-based-development`).
column5: Continuous integration (CI) is the combination of practicing trunk-based development and maintaining a suite of fast automated tests that run after each commit to trunk to make sure the system is always working.

column3: If the CI process fails, developers must stop what they are doing either to fix the problem immediately or to revert the change if it cannot be fixed in a few minutes (`dora-capabilities-trunk#how-to-implement-trunk-based-development`).
column5: This means that if the CI process fails, developers must stop what they’re doing either to fix the problem immediately or to revert the change if it can’t be fixed in a few minutes.

column3: DORA data from 2016 and 2017 shows that teams achieve higher software delivery and operational performance if they have three or fewer active branches in the application's code repository (`dora-capabilities-trunk#how-to-implement-trunk-based-development`).
column5: Have three or fewer active branches in the application’s code repository.

column3: The same DORA analysis points to merging branches to trunk at least once a day (`dora-capabilities-trunk#how-to-implement-trunk-based-development`).
column5: Merge branches to trunk at least once a day.

column3: The same DORA analysis points to having no code freezes and no integration phases (`dora-capabilities-trunk#how-to-implement-trunk-based-development`).
column5: Don’t have code freezes and don’t have integration phases.

column3: Flyway migrations are SQL scripts that capture schema and data changes and should be tracked in version control (`flyway-migrations#migrations`).
column5: These are SQL scripts that can capture schema and data changes (eg., CREATE, ALTER, INSERT, UPDATE, etc.). They should be tracked in version control.

column3: The same migration scripts run in the same order on each environment, which gives a repeatable deployment process (`flyway-migrations#migrations`).
column5: The same scripts will be run in the same order on each environment, which gives you a repeatable deployment process.

column3: Flyway Migrate scans the filesystem or classpath for available migrations, compares them to the migrations applied to the database and, if any difference is found, migrates the database to close the gap (`flyway-migrations#Migrations-Migrate`).
column5: It will scan the filesystem or your classpath for available migrations. It will compare them to the migrations that have been applied to the database. If any difference is found, it will migrate the database to close the gap.

column3: Flyway Migrate should preferably be executed on application startup to avoid any incompatibilities between the database and the expectations of the code (`flyway-migrations#Migrations-Migrate`).
column5: Migrate should preferably be executed on application startup to avoid any incompatibilities between the database and the expectations of the code.

column3: Executing Migrate is idempotent and can be done safely regardless of the current version of the schema (`flyway-migrations#Migrations-Migrate`).
column5: Executing migrate is idempotent and can be done safely regardless of the current version of the schema.

column3: Flyway adds a schema history table to your schema to keep track of which migrations have been applied, when and by whom (`flyway-migrations#Migrations-Schemahistory`).
column5: To keep track of which migrations have already been applied when and by whom, Flyway adds a schema history table to your schema.

column3: By default Flyway wraps the execution of each migration script in a single transaction and applies them in order (`flyway-migrations#Migrations-Transactionhandling`).
column5: By default Flyway wraps the execution of each migration script in a single transaction and applies them in order.

column3: A changeset is the basic unit of change in Liquibase (`liquibase-changeset#main-header`).
column5: A changeset is the basic unit of change in Liquibase.

column3: By default, Liquibase runs a changeset as a single transaction, and the `runInTransaction` attribute modifies this behavior (`liquibase-changeset#main-header`).
column5: By default, Liquibase runs changesets as a single transaction. You can modify this behavior with the runInTransaction attribute.

column3: Once a changeset has run, Liquibase does not re-run it unless `runAlways` or `runOnChange` is specified for that changeset (`liquibase-changeset#main-header`).
column5: Once you run a changeset, Liquibase does not re-run it unless you specify runAlways or runOnChange for that changeset.

column3: DORA has identified five software delivery performance metrics that provide an effective way of measuring the outcomes of the software delivery process (`dora-metrics#by-nathen-harvey`).
column5: DORA has identified five software delivery performance metrics that provide an effective way of measuring the outcomes of the software delivery process.

column3: The metrics shifted from the original four keys to the current five-metric model (`dora-metrics#by-nathen-harvey`).
column5: These metrics have evolved alongside the technology landscape: shifting from the original four keys to the current five-metric model.

column3: The metrics divide into those that show the throughput of software changes and those that show the instability of software changes (`dora-metrics#throughput-and-instability`).
column5: They can be divided into metrics that show the throughput of software changes, and metrics that show instability of software changes.

column3: Throughput is a measure of how many changes can move through the system over a period of time (`dora-metrics#throughput`).
column5: Throughput is a measure of how many changes can move through the system over a period of time.

column3: DORA measures throughput with three factors: change lead time, deployment frequency and failed deployment recovery time (`dora-metrics#throughput`).
column5: DORA uses three factors to measure software delivery throughput:

column3: Change lead time is the amount of time it takes for a change to go from committed to version control to deployed in production (`dora-metrics#throughput`).
column5: Change lead time: The amount of time it takes for a change to go from committed to version control to deployed in production.

column3: Failed deployment recovery time is the time it takes to recover from a deployment that fails and requires immediate intervention (`dora-metrics#throughput`).
column5: Failed deployment recovery time: The time it takes to recover from a deployment that fails and requires immediate intervention.

column3: Instability is a measure of how well the software deployments go (`dora-metrics#instability`).
column5: Instability is a measure of how well the software deployments go.

column3: DORA measures instability with two factors: change fail rate and deployment rework rate (`dora-metrics#instability`).
column5: DORA uses two factors to measure software delivery instability:

column3: Change fail rate is the ratio of deployments that require immediate intervention following a deployment, likely resulting in a rollback or a hotfix (`dora-metrics#instability`).
column5: Change fail rate: The ratio of deployments that require immediate intervention following a deployment.

column3: Deployment rework rate is the ratio of deployments that are unplanned but happen as a result of an incident in production (`dora-metrics#instability`).
column5: Deployment rework rate: The ratio of deployments that are unplanned but happen as a result of an incident in production.
